title: New Year & Little Resolutions
strapline: A fresh year, a fresh start — what would you like to learn to do?
intent: Marking a new year gives children a gentle first sense of time passing, looking back and looking forward.
Choosing a little 'I'd like to learn to...' goal builds self-awareness, hope and the will to keep trying.
Talking about what they can do now that they couldn't before grows pride, confidence and a sense of growing up.
New year celebrations from different cultures widen knowledge and honour the many new years families keep.
The theme is a warm springboard for aspiration, goal-setting and celebrating effort.
implementation: Open a talk about the new year: 'A whole new year is starting — what would you love to learn to do this year?'
Help each child name one small, real goal — do up my own coat, write my name, ride the trike — and record it warmly.
Celebrate how much they've grown: 'What can you do now that you couldn't when you were little?'
Bring in new year celebrations from around the world — different dates, foods, lanterns, fireworks — and honour the ones families keep.
Revisit the goals through the year and celebrate every step, however small.
Keep it light and hopeful — resolutions for tinies are about aspiration and pride, never pressure.
key_questions: What would you love to learn to do this year?
What can you do now that you couldn't do when you were a baby?
How could we help you learn to do that?
How does your family welcome the new year?
How did it feel when you finally managed something tricky?

impact.text: Children set a small goal and show the will to keep trying at it.
Children talk about how they've grown and what they can do now.
Children learn that different families and cultures welcome new years in different ways.
Children talk about their feelings and hopes for the year.
Children take pride in effort and in reaching their goals.

enhancements: A 'this year I'd like to learn to...' goal board with each child's aspiration.
A 'look how I've grown' display comparing baby photos with now.
New-year celebrations from around the world — lanterns, fireworks pictures, foods.
A revisiting routine to celebrate goals reached through the year.
A mark-making table for children to draw or 'write' their own resolution.

playing_exploring: Children explore new-year celebrations and materials with curiosity.
They engage with the idea of a fresh start in their own way.
active_learning: Children hold on to a personal goal and keep working towards it.
They take pride in the effort and in progress made.
creating_thinking: Children reflect on how they've grown and what they'd like to learn.
They connect new year to their own family's traditions and hopes.
